text.insert: Knowledge processing is one standing pipeline from durable input through classification, leased execution, validation, and accepted publication. Queue rows carry dispatch and retry truth; domain records carry accepted evidence, so a succeeded dispatch points to publication evidence instead of becoming that evidence.

steps.text: Enqueue a typed source artifact with stable source identity
Classify the authority required to process and publish it
Claim the durable job under a fenced lease
Move from `claimed` to `running` when execution begins
Return retryable failures to `waiting` with durable backoff
Materialize learnings, attempts, or source records into staging
Validate evidence, anchors, and idempotency keys
Accept at the governing authority boundary and advance the knowledge revision
Expose the coherent revision to subsequent workers

text.insert: The game view composes the queue backlog with the latest accepted revision. It is an operator read model, not a separate workflow slot or durable knowledge aggregate.

fields.name: jobs
fields.description: Knowledge-kind dispatch rows projected from the shared jobs table.

fields.name: queued
fields.description: Jobs eligible for a future claim.

fields.name: claimed
fields.description: Jobs owned by a lease but not yet executing.

fields.name: running
fields.description: Jobs executing under a fenced lease.

fields.name: waiting
fields.description: Jobs blocked by a dependency or retry time.

fields.name: failed
fields.description: Jobs whose latest terminal outcome failed.

fields.name: oldest_pending_at
fields.description: Age anchor for the visible backlog.

fields.name: active_lease
fields.description: Current claim fencing projected from claimed or running rows.

fields.name: recent_failures
fields.description: Bounded failure evidence without mutation of accepted knowledge.

text.insert: Live intake processes one newly available packet; historical backfill executes a finite manifest of the same typed batches. Both use current-checkout anchoring, evidence validation, and the same acceptance boundaries. The worker-finished enqueue hook is implemented but disabled unless a run enables `--librarian-on-worker-finish`.
